summary: A 1939-41 Civilian Conservation Corps lookout on a cinder cone in Lava Beds National Monument. No longer in regular fire use; visitors can hike to the top.

facts.design: Rustic one-story wood-frame cab with a basement and lava rock veneer; Osborne fire finder inside

staffing.status: no longer in regular use (NPS); register describes May to September staffing

access.note: The National Park Service says visitors are welcome to hike to the top. Sources do not say whether the cab interior is open.

visit.trail_note: About 0.7 miles (1.1 km) each way on foot; no water at the top; stay on the trail and do not cut switchbacks.

facts.agency: National Park Service - Lava Beds National Monument

events.note: CCC construction 1939 onward. NPS says the lookout and trail were built 1939 to 1941; the register says the summers of 1939 and 1940; the nomination says 1940-1941.
Roger Reid was the first to staff the lookout
Electric power line installed in the 1950s; exact year not given
Power line removed in the 1980s (mid-1980s per the register); exact year not given
Interior stripped, rotten boards and sheetrock replaced, June and July 1994, from about $50,000 received in 1993
Added to the National Register September 5, 2017 per Wikipedia; the register's narrative says on the Register by 1992
Registered October 27, 2019 as NHLR US 1358, CA 181

corrections.why: The National Register nomination describes the lookout as one-story with a basement. The record's two-story label may count the basement level. Judgement call for the editor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the CCC worked in the summers of 1939 and 1940. The NPS says the lookout and trail were built 1939 to 1941. The nomination dates construction to 1940-1941. The story gives the NPS range and notes the narrower nomination dates.
Wikipedia gives September 5, 2017. The register's narrative says the building was on the Register by 1992. The story reports both and does not choose.

The register says the lookout is staffed roughly May to September. The NPS page (updated December 2023) says it is no longer in regular use, and the nomination calls it still operational. The story leads with the NPS page as the most recent source.

The register gives 5,270 ft (1,606 m). The NPS says the recorded figure is 5293 ft and its modern figure is 5302 ft (1616 m). The record keeps the register value; the editor may prefer the NPS figure.

notes_for_editor: A search result (not a fetched page) mentioned a closure after winter wind damage and a later reopening of the road and trail. I could not verify it in a fetched page, so the story omits it. Check Lava Beds alerts before publishing. The kind correction is a judgement call based on the nomination's wording. The staffing as_of date is the NPS page's last-updated date, not a staffing confirmation.
